1.pericope_label: And he shewed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and Satan standing at his right hand to resist him. And the Lord said unto Satan, The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan; even the Lord that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?

schools.summary: Traces the philology of the high priest's name through its contractions into the Greek form, treats him as the representative of the people, and takes the fire for the captivity's penal suffering.
Set the vision against the discouragement of a small return and a hindered building, and read the high priest typically rather than personally.
Give the historical occasion of the opposition to the rebuilding and identify the angel of the Lord with Christ.
Contrasts how the high priest appeared before men with how he stood before God, and pairs the two men of that name as figures of the one to come.

debates.question: Is Joshua seen personally or as a figure?

positions.position: Better typically than personally, as representing the state of the priesthood under the second temple, or the church.
As representative of the people, in the guilt as in the pardon and the promise.
Both: the prophet knew the man, but had to be shown in vision how he stood before God, since men are as they are with God and not as they appear to the world.
Historically, as the high priest whose restored ministry would encourage a people opposed in their building.

debates.question: What does the formula of rebuke imply about the angel of the Lord?

positions.position: He is Christ, the Lord of the angels, to whom even the high priests of Aaron's order were accountable.
Nothing: the words are a standing formula for threatening divine judgment, from which no conclusion may be drawn about the relation of the persons.

outliers.claim: Sets the vision against its occasion, that only a small part of the nation had returned and enemies at once hindered the building, so the faithful must look for more than the aspect of things warranted and to a power God purposely withheld to try their patience.
Traces the forms of the high priest's name, the name of the Saviour of the world, from its oldest Hebrew form through successive contractions to the Greek form that yields Jesus.

themes: And he shewed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and Satan standing at his right hand to resist him.

3.pericope_label: Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel. And he answered and spake unto those that stood before him, saying, Take away the filthy garments from him. And unto him he said, Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment. And I said, Let them set a fair mitre upon his head. So they set a fair mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments. And the angel of the Lord stood by. And the angel of the Lord protested unto Joshua, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by.

schools.summary: Explain the courtiers who stand by as angels of inferior grade, correct the tense of the clothing to an aorist of the immediate past, and say why the prophet interrupts to ask for the mitre.
Weigh whose words the request for the mitre is, and note that the Angel annexed an oath to his word to confirm the promises.
Identify the speaker as Christ and the attendants as ministerial angels, and extend the conditions of the charge from the priest to the whole people.
States that all whom God calls to an office he finds fit or makes so, and reads the promises as looking forward to Christ.

debates.question: What do the filthy garments stand for?

positions.position: A particular sin of the high priest or his sons, aggravated by the accuser.
The forlorn and sinful condition of the whole people and a defiled priesthood.
Ritual unfitness to appear before God as priest, a symbol of the guilt and defilement of sin.
The emblem of a poor or sinful state.

outliers.claim: Explains the prophet's interruption as prompted by a fear that the change of raiment might signify only the removal of the priest's own guilt, the mitre mattering because the golden plate inscribed with holiness to the Lord was fastened to it.
Draws from the change of garments that what angels could not take away Christ did, removing the filth of sin with both its guilt and its stain.

8.pericope_label: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH. For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes: behold, I will engrave the graving thereof, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree.

schools.summary: Objects on grammar that the stone must be a noun of multitude meaning the material stones of the house, since otherwise the following words should read upon that stone.
Denies the stone is the plummet or the foundation stone laid by Zerubbabel, making it Christ laid before the priest to build his faith upon.
Reject the identification of the Branch with Zerubbabel, take the seven eyes for providence or for Christ's knowledge, and read the closing day as one of liberty and tranquillity.
Explains why the promises to the priest rise at once to Christ, since the virtue of his own priesthood was derived from that one.

debates.question: What is the stone laid before Joshua?

positions.position: Christ, the stone of Israel whom the builders refused, laid before the priest to build his faith upon.
The temple's foundation stone in allusion, but Christ and none other in signification.
A particular stone pointed out, bearing seven eyes placed to look many ways.
Not one stone but the stones: the singular is a noun of multitude for the material stones of the house, since otherwise the text should read upon that stone.

debates.question: What does it mean that they are men wondered at?

positions.position: Men of sign, to whom signs are given and for whom miracles are wrought, or else men accustomed to interpret enigmatical prophecies.
Figurative men, whose office and ministration prefigured Christ.
Men wondered at by unbelieving Jews, for the labour and expense of attempting such a building.

outliers.claim: Reports that an archbishop understood the Branch of Zerubbabel as heir to the throne of Judah, notes that the Chaldee reads my servant the Messiah, and gives his own judgment against the Zerubbabel reading.
Argues that the high priest himself needed to understand the priesthood of Christ, since all the virtue and usefulness of his own office to the church was derived from it.
